add.title: Seven transgender prison inmates awarded €5,000 each in damages for 'truly disgusting' treatment (Malta Today)
add.summary: Malta Today (29 May 2018): the Maltese civil court (Judge Silvio Meli) awarded seven transgender inmates of Corradino prison €5,000 each (€4,000 for breach of rights plus €1,000 for damage to personal dignity) after the prison authorities held them in the male section, where they shared cells with male inmates, were forced to use the men's showers (often forgoing washing) and suffered insults and 'continuous sexual abuse and violence'. The court found the authorities had 'knowingly and repeatedly' placed them in situations of high risk of sexual and psychological violence; the only alternative offered, transfer to the female section, would have cost them the work and study opportunities they needed to pay for hormone therapy, and female inmates and warders were said to be hostile, so they stayed in the male section. The director of prisons was ordered to pay; the Aditus Foundation human-rights NGO represented the seven women.

add.title: The lived experiences of transgender inmates at Malta's Correctional Service Agency (Oriana Vidal, University of Malta, 2024)
add.summary: University of Malta master's dissertation (Oriana Vidal, 2024) interviewing four current and former transgender/gender-diverse inmates of Malta's Correctional Service Agency (CSA), a cohort spanning the last 25 years. It records that after Malta's 2013 gender-law reform CSA practice allowed TGD inmates to transfer to the female section, whereas earlier practice had segregated them in a separate dormitory (staff described the rationale as 'the risks of pregnancies'); participants now receive individual cells in the female section but report residual misgendering by officers (masculine birth names), gender-appropriate clothing and healthcare gaps, and conclude that CSA practice, policies and procedures lag Malta's progressive national gender-identity law. It also cites the 2018 newspaper report (Agius, Malta Today) of seven TGD inmates winning a court award after rights breaches including strip searches, showering-privacy issues and being treated as males.
